# Provenance + integrity record for the vendored ui scripts (#577 — the #332
# recipe's ui variant). The sha256s below are ENFORCED by ui/vendor_test.go
# (the uiVendorScripts pin table). An upgrade is the full recipe, in ONE
# commit: the vendored blob + the sha256 here + the pin table in
# ui/vendor_test.go + the go:embed list in ui/embed.go + the handleAsset case
# list in internal/server/server.go + the /assets script tags in summary.html
# and disclosure.html. The #577 customManagers in renovate.json read the
# version from those REFERENCE files (config:recommended's
# :ignoreModulesAndTests preset adds **/vendor/** to ignorePaths; the
# standard ignores are deliberately not overridden — provenance here is
# hand-maintained, same as internal/report/vendor/).
#
# WHY NO BREAKOUT GUARD (deliberate difference from the report variant): the
# report blobs are inlined as template.JS/template.CSS and need the
# </script>/</style> hazard checks; these ui blobs are served as EXTERNAL
# responses (Content-Type application/javascript + nosniff, handleAsset) —
# the html/template escape/breakout class has no reach here. The guards that
# DO transfer are the sha256 lock and the versioned-name invariants in
# ui/vendor_test.go.
#
# LIMITATION (recorded, #577): DOMPurify is the sole XSS sanitizer for the
# untrusted-markdown render path of summary.html + disclosure.html; no
# Content-Security-Policy header is set anywhere in internal/server/ (the
# securityHeaders wrapper sets X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options,
# Referrer-Policy, COOP, CORP, Permissions-Policy and
# X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies — a CSP would additionally need nonces
# or hashes for the templates' inline <script> and <style> blocks: a design
# change, deliberately out of this fix's scope).
#
# marked-12.0.2.min.js
#   source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/marked@12.0.2/marked.min.js
#   npm anchor: registry.npmjs.org/marked/-/marked-12.0.2.tgz
#   dist.integrity (of the .tgz, not of the inner file): sha512-qXUm7e/YKFoqFPYPa3Ukg9xlI5cyAtGmyEIzMfW//m6kXwCy2Ps9DYf5ioijFKQ8qyuscrHoY04iJGctu2Kg0Q==
#   sha256: 15fabce5b65898b32b03f5ed25e9f891a729ad4c0d6d877110a7744aa847a894
#   verified: 2026-09-12 — the pre-#577 blob (as marked.min.js) is
#         byte-identical to the official 12.0.2 dist (compared against the
#         tarball's package/marked.min.js); this entry is a RENAME, not a
#         re-vendor. The six-major gap to marked 18.x is a separate
#         re-vendor decision: it gets its own PR when the notifier surfaces
#         it (no allowedVersions cap — the artifact channel is live). No
#         published advisory covers 12.0.2 (the 18.x OOM advisory's reviewed
#         range is [18.0.0, 18.0.2); its prose hedges "potentially earlier
#         versions" — unverified for 12.x, so the advisory record is the
#         current state, not proof of safety).
#
# dompurify-3.4.15.min.js
#   source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dompurify@3.4.15/dist/purify.min.js
#   npm anchor: registry.npmjs.org/dompurify/-/dompurify-3.4.15.tgz
#   dist.integrity (of the .tgz, not of the inner file): sha512-EUBjM+B+lkDE41iE82DDSCfkoPGfXx8IxFxPMjNzm/Uk4xDet77rTN9wqlxlVg71kK7XGuUMv6wUxJUwwv+Xyw==
#   sha256: f263b05369e050fa175d4ecb9c9358eb4253602d510297adfb31df48b2f1c4d5
#   verified: 2026-09-12 — the tarball sha512 was re-derived and MATCHED the
#         registry dist.integrity at write time; the committed bytes are the
#         tarball's dist/purify.min.js, verbatim. Currency bump from 3.4.13
#         (the pre-#577 blob was itself genuine — byte-identical to the
#         3.4.13 dist, and 3.4.13 is the version that fixed the
#         GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 advisory). 3.4.14 and 3.4.15 carry no advisory
#         ids; upstream's notes name bypass preconditions (risky tags
#         allow-listed; XML-content clobbering) that this app's inert
#         MD_SANITIZE allowlist does not meet — this is a hygiene/currency
#         bump of the sole sanitizer, not a claim that a known exploit is
#         closed. The trailing sourceMappingURL comment references a map the
#         /assets route never serves (allowlisted) — cosmetic, kept verbatim
#         for byte fidelity.
